      "claim": "Option (C) states that whether the model is good can be determined by comparing the SRF and the PRF. Since the PRF is unknown, we cannot directly compare them. Actually, usually, we evaluate the model by checking if the SRF is a good estimator of the PRF. But we can't see the PRF. Let's look closer at standard textbook definitions. Often, 'goodness' is assessed via diagnostics on the SRF (R-squared, residuals). Comparing SRF and PRF is impossible because PRF is unknown. Wait, let's look at the options again. Is there a better interpretation? \n\nLet's re-read standard definitions. \n(A) PRF is estimated model -> False, SRF is estimated.\n(B) PRF used to infer SRF -> False, SRF estimates PRF.\n(D) PRF is description of process -> True. The PRF *is* the mathematical representation of the data generating process.\n(C) Model goodness determined by comparing SRF and PRF -> False, because PRF is unknown. You cannot compare what you don't know. You assess the SRF's properties (unbiasedness, efficiency) to infer it approximates the PRF well.\n\nTherefore, (D) is the most theoretically accurate statement among the choices, as it correctly identifies the nature of the PRF.",
